title: SSL Hybrid
summary: A baseline average with a range channel, three SSL lines that flip sides on closes, ATR bands, exit arrows, large-candle diamonds and a risk table.
description:
SSL Hybrid combines several trend lines built from one menu of averages. The **Baseline** is an average of the close over the `Baseline Length`, of the type picked in `Baseline Type`: SMA, EMA, DEMA, TEMA, LSMA (the linear regression value), WMA, MF (a modular filter), VAMA (the EMA plus the middle of the source's highest and lowest distance from it), TMA, HMA, JMA, Kijun v2 (midpoints of the high and low range), EDSMA (an average whose speed follows a super smoother of the two-bar change) or McGinley. Every exponential average starts from its first value. A channel sits around the baseline at `Channel Multiplier` times an exponential average of the true range, or of the bar's high minus its low.

Each SSL line is one average of the highs and one of the lows. When the close goes above the average of the highs the side turns up and the line follows the average of the lows; when it goes below the average of the lows the side turns down and the line follows the average of the highs; between them the side holds. **SSL1** uses the baseline's type and length, **SSL2** its own type and length, and a third, the exit line, sets the arrows and is not drawn.

The average true range is the true range smoothed by `ATR Smoothing`. It gives the optional **+ATR** and **-ATR** bands around the close, and its percentile over the `Risk Lookback Period` (the share of earlier values at or below the latest) sets the transparency of the bullish and bearish colours, so lines and candles fade as volatility rises.
howToRead:
Candles and the baseline are coloured bullish while the close is above the channel, bearish while it is below, and grey inside it, which marks a market without direction. SSL1 is coloured by the close's side of it. SSL2 is coloured bullish on a continuation: the close above both the baseline and SSL2, with SSL2 within `Continuation ATR Criteria` average true ranges of the close (and bearish for the mirror case).

An up arrow below a bar marks the close crossing above the exit line and a down arrow above a bar the close crossing below it, read as the point to leave a short or a long. A diamond above a bar marks a candle body larger than one average true range while the baseline is within one average true range of the close, a possible false breakout. The table in the bottom right shows the latest bar's risk level, how far the close is from the baseline, the volatility percentile and the average true range. Lines and arrows react only after the averages move, so they confirm a trend rather than predict one.

settings.label: Display Mode
settings.description: Which lines are drawn: the baseline, the SSL lines, the exit arrows, or all of them.

settings.label: Color Bars
settings.description: Colour the candles bullish, bearish or grey by the close's side of the baseline channel.

settings.label: Show Signal Diamonds
settings.description: Mark candles whose body is larger than one average true range while the baseline is within one average true range.

settings.label: Show Risk Table
settings.description: Show the table of risk level, entry distance, volatility percentile and average true range.

settings.label: Bullish Color
settings.description: The colour of the bullish side, faded as the volatility percentile rises.

settings.label: Bearish Color
settings.description: The colour of the bearish side, faded as the volatility percentile rises.

settings.label: Baseline Type
settings.description: The average used for the baseline, its channel and SSL1.

settings.label: Baseline Length
settings.description: Bars in the baseline average, in SSL1 and in the channel's range average.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series the channel is centred on. The baseline itself averages the close.

settings.label: Show Baseline Channel
settings.description: Draw the channel lines and the shading around the baseline.

settings.label: Channel Multiplier
settings.description: The channel's half width as a multiple of the average range. Larger values widen the grey zone.

settings.label: Use True Range for Channel
settings.description: Measure the channel with the true range, which includes gaps from the previous close, rather than the bar's high minus its low.

settings.label: SSL2 Type
settings.description: The average used for the SSL2 line.

settings.label: SSL2 Length
settings.description: Bars in the SSL2 averages. Short values make SSL2 follow price closely.

settings.label: Continuation ATR Criteria
settings.description: How many average true ranges SSL2 may sit from the close for a continuation to count.

settings.label: Exit Type
settings.description: The average used for the exit line whose crossings draw the arrows.

settings.label: Exit Length
settings.description: Bars in the exit line's averages. Shorter values give earlier and more frequent arrows.

settings.label: ATR Period
settings.description: Bars in the average true range.

settings.label: ATR Multiplier
settings.description: The distance of the ATR bands from the close, in average true ranges.

settings.label: ATR Smoothing
settings.description: The average applied to the true range: RMA, SMA, EMA or WMA.

settings.label: Show ATR Bands
settings.description: Draw the +ATR and -ATR bands around the close.

settings.label: Risk Lookback Period
settings.description: Earlier bars the volatility percentile compares the latest average true range with.

settings.label: Risk Sensitivity
settings.description: The power the percentile is raised to before it sets the transparency. Higher values fade the colours only at the highest volatility.

settings.label: Enable Risk Gradient
settings.description: Fade the bullish and bearish colours as volatility rises. Off, they are always solid.

settings.label: Phase
settings.description: JMA phase from -100 to 100; higher values let the JMA lead more and overshoot more.

settings.label: Power
settings.description: JMA power, the exponent of its smoothing factor. Higher values make it react faster.

settings.label: Kijun MOD Divider
settings.description: Kijun v2 divides its length by this for its shorter range midpoint.

settings.label: Volatility Lookback Length
settings.description: Bars over which VAMA takes the highest and lowest distance of the source from its average.

settings.label: Beta
settings.description: How far the MF filter leans toward the envelope on the side of the last breakout, from 0 to 1.

settings.label: Feedback
settings.description: Blend the MF filter's previous value into its input, which smooths it further.

settings.label: Feedback Weighting
settings.description: With feedback on, the weight of the source in the MF filter's input; the rest is its previous value.

settings.label: Super Smoother Filter Length
settings.description: The length of the super smoother inside EDSMA.

settings.label: Super Smoother Filter Poles
settings.description: Two or three poles for the super smoother inside EDSMA. Three poles smooth more and lag more.

faq.q: Why do some candles keep their own colour on the first bars?
faq.a: The bullish and bearish colours take their transparency from the volatility percentile, which needs the average true range plus `Risk Lookback Period` earlier values. Until then those colours do not exist, so a candle above or below the channel keeps its own colour (one inside it is still grey). Turn off `Enable Risk Gradient` to colour them from the start.

faq.q: Why does the SSL2 line start far from price?
faq.a: The default SSL2 type is JMA, whose smoothing stages start from zero, so it climbs to price over the first few bars. Other types instead start once their window is full.

faq.q: What does the exit line do if it is not drawn?
faq.a: It is a third SSL line, of `Exit Type` and `Exit Length`. The arrows mark the close crossing it, and the exit alerts fire on the same crossings.

Exit long and exit short, SSL2 buy and sell continuation, price above the upper channel or below the lower channel, price crossing the baseline, a high risk entry, a false breakout warning and extreme volatility.
